prerequisites: Mathematics and programming skills corresponding to the mathematics and programming modules of the respective study programs.
Basic knowledge in operating systems, computer architectures, or microcomputer technology are helpful.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire broad knowledge about embedded systems, subject to the constraints of limited resources and hardware dependencies. In particular, they will know the processes of modern software development for these systems.

Students will possess the knowledge of how software for embedded systems is structured. They will know the design process and tools for creating software for these systems. They will understand the concepts for testing embedded software.
Students can evaluate, select, and apply the tools that support the design process for embedded systems.
They understand how embedded systems integrate into an overall system.
Students can design and develop embedded systems from specification to a finished product, considering economic and ecological constraints.

Students can specify suitable embedded systems for a given task, create an appropriate software concept for it, and select necessary tools and test environments. They proceed methodically and structured, using professional aids. They can represent problem statements and their proposed solutions argumentatively to experts.
Students can develop solutions in a team, taking into account the different competencies and perspectives of other team members.

syllabus_topics: Program implementation: Booting, Cross-Compiling, Linking, Loading, Remote-Debugging
Real-time operating system kernels: Process management, Scheduling, Process communication, Interrupt processing, Hardware abstraction
Programming of embedded systems using the example of simple applications with and without a real-time operating system.
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is chosen by the instructors (either a written exam or a project report). For a written project report, a workload of 40 hours is expected for its creation, as well as participation in the presentation of the reports. The experimental work is an ungraded examination performance, consisting of approximately 5 experiments, for each of which several appointments may be required.
